title: Hotpath threshold correlation - data extract for queueing & throttles (2026-10-20)
summary: Data pull for correlating service-level hotpath threshold crossings with regional GPU saturation, queue depth, and automatic throttle events. Purpose: produce a compact dataset for the incident RCA and to feed the diagnostic notebook for model routing fallback evaluation.
purpose: Produce joined timeseries and event slices that link: (1) low-latency hotpath SLO breaches, (2) per-GPU queue depth and busy_ratio, (3) autoscaling/throttle events and policy decisions, and (4) model variant fallbacks. Intended consumers: infra oncall, serving-runtime, SRE and product incident owners.
sampling_windows: Primary slice: 2026-10-18T02:00:00Z -> 2026-10-19T06:00:00Z (12h before high-latency spike through 24h after)
Burst windows: auto-detected contiguous intervals where hotpath_slo_violation_rate > 0.5% for >= 5m
key_metrics_table: hotpath_slo_violation_rate | pct per minute | 1m | SLO = p95 latency > 120ms for hotpath route
gpu_util_busy_ratio | mean per GPU | 30s | from fleet telemetry (nvlink aggregated)
gpu_queue_depth | p50,p90,p99 across GPUs | 30s | kernel queue + runtime request queue
throttle_event_count | count per region | 1m | includes automatic and manual throttle actions
active_batch_size | mean tokens/batch | 30s | derived from serving runtime trace tags
model_fallback_count | count by variant | 1m | when primary model variant rejected due to capacity
raw_queries:
-- join hotpath SLOs to GPU telemetry (bigquery)
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(h.ts, MINUTE) AS ts_min,
  h.region,
  COUNTIF(h.p95_latency_ms > 120) / COUNT(*) AS hotpath_violation_rate,
  AVG(g.busy_ratio) AS avg_gpu_busy,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(g.queue_depth, 100)[OFFSET(90)] AS q90_queue_depth
FROM
  `prod.telemetry.hotpath_latency_v2` h
LEFT JOIN
  `prod.telemetry.gpu_fleet_metrics_v1` g
  ON h.region = g.region AND TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(g.ts, MINUTE) = TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(h.ts, MINUTE)
WHERE
  h.ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-10-18T02:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-10-19T06:00:00Z')
GROUP BY ts_min, region
ORDER BY ts_min

-- extract throttle events and correlate to request overflow
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(t.ts, MINUTE) AS ts_min,
  t.region,
  t.throttle_type,
  COUNT(*) AS events,
  SUM(t.requests_rejected) AS requests_rejected
FROM
  `prod.events.throttle_actions` t
WHERE
  t.ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-10-18T02:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-10-19T06:00:00Z')
GROUP BY ts_min, region, throttle_type
ORDER BY ts_min

-- get per-request traces for hotpath requests hitting fallback
SELECT
  r.request_id,
  r.ts,
  r.region,
  r.latency_ms,
  r.model_variant_requested,
  r.model_variant_served,
  r.serving_node_id,
  r.queue_time_ms
FROM
  `prod.traces.request_level` r
WHERE
  r.is_hotpath = TRUE
  AND r.ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-10-18T02:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-10-19T06:00:00Z')
  AND r.queue_time_ms > 10
LIMIT 10000
top_findings: Temporal alignment: the first notable cluster of hotpath SLO breaches (2026-10-18T03:14Z -> 03:38Z) lines up with a sharp regional increase in avg_gpu_busy for us-west1 (+22pp) and a simultaneous rise in p99 queue_depth.

Autoscaler latency: scaling decisions for Dedicated pools in us-west1 showed a median decision latency of ~45s (beyond target 15s) during the spike, causing transient undersupply before extra nodes registered.
Batching behavior: mean active_batch_size increased by ~1.8x during the event for long-sequence workloads; higher batching reduced per-token cost but increased tail queueing on hotpath requests.

Throttle pattern: two automated throttle bursts (03:20Z and 03:31Z) were correlated with policy threshold crossings tied to per-pool queue_length > 500; the throttle implementation rejected entire request batches instead of shedding low-priority replicas first.

Model fallback: 13% of hotpath requests were routed to smaller quantized variants during the incident; these fallbacks had lower p95 latency but higher rejection rate for large prompt sizes, contributing to user-visible errors.
Regional imbalance: europe-west2 saw modest load increases but did not receive cross-region failover due to routing policy set to prefer region affinity for hotpath, limiting spillover headroom.
Telemetry gaps: there is a 5–12s jitter window between serving runtime queue_time metrics and fleet-level GPU busy_ratio, complicating precise causality attribution for sub-30s spikes.
recommended_actions: Short term (1–7d): implement an emergency policy to prefer shedding non-hotpath workloads before throttling hotpath routes; change throttle implementation to operate at request-level granularity for affected pools.

Short term: add a fast-path autoscaler hook that forces a cold-started node to register as "available" for routing earlier (soft register) while full health checks finish, reducing decision latency impact.
Medium term (2–6w): introduce dynamic routing override that allows controlled cross-region spillover when regional headroom < 10% and latency SLOs for hotpath are degrading beyond threshold.
Medium term: align batch-size controller with hotpath prioritization so that active_batch_size heuristics consider request priority tags and avoid increasing batch size for hotpath-dominant slices.

Long term (quarter): instrument sub-minute synchronized telemetry (micro-buckets) between runtime and fleet to remove the 5–12s jitter window; evaluate event-driven streaming of queue-depth signals to autoscaler.
Monitoring: add a composite alert that fires when (hotpath_p95 > 120ms) AND (avg_gpu_busy > 75%) in a region for >=2m; route to infra-oncall plus serving-runtime oncall.
